headline: Excite Rejected the Chance to Buy Google in 1999

sentences.text: Larry Page and Sergey Brin started a search site.
They wanted to sell their young business in 1999.
The two students asked for one million dollars.
A big internet company named Excite said no.
Today Google has a value of over one trillion dollars.

grammar.title: Infinitive as Object
grammar.note: When verbs like 'want' take another action as their direct object, use 'to' + base verb. Here, 'to sell' shows what they wanted.

grammar.title: Prepositional Phrase Modifying Noun
grammar.note: The preposition 'of' connects a noun phrase to specify the amount or type of 'value'. It gives extra details about the target noun.

sentences.text: Two college students built a tool to find online information.
Larry Page and Sergey Brin wanted to sell it in 1999.
They asked an internet company called Excite to buy their work.
The young men lowered their price, but Excite still refused.
Excite will never get another chance to buy that great business.
Google is now one of the most valuable companies on Earth.

grammar.focus: asked an internet company called Excite to buy
grammar.title: Ask Someone to Do Something
grammar.note: This structure follows 'ask + object + to-infinitive'. It is used to express requesting someone to complete an action.

grammar.focus: one of the most valuable companies
grammar.title: Superlative with One Of
grammar.note: Use 'one of the + superlative + plural noun' to pick out a single entity from a group of top-ranked items.

sentences.text: In 1999, two graduate students at Stanford University created an early search engine.
Larry Page and Sergey Brin found that their project took too much time from studies.
Therefore, they decided to sell their technology, which helped people find online pages.
The creators approached an internet firm called Excite with an offer of one million dollars.
An advisor helped lower the price to $750,000 so Excite would agree to buy it.
However, Excite manager George Bell rejected the offer because he disliked their system rules.
Since that famous decision, Google has grown into a company worth over a trillion dollars.

grammar.title: Noun Clause as Object
grammar.note: The conjunction 'that' introduces a whole clause functioning as the direct object of the verb 'found'.

grammar.title: Bare Infinitive after Help
grammar.note: The verb 'help' can take a bare infinitive (verb without 'to') as its complement, meaning 'helped to lower'.

grammar.title: Present Perfect Tense
grammar.note: The present perfect 'has + past participle' connects a past action or process to current reality.

sentences.text: Before becoming an internet giant, Google was a modest university research project in California.
In 1999, founders Larry Page and Sergey Brin attempted to sell their search engine to focus on schoolwork.
The pair initially approached Excite, a popular web directory, offering their technology for $1 million.
When Excite showed hesitation, an investor helped negotiate the proposed acquisition price down to $750,000.
However, chief executive officer George Bell turned down the offer during negotiations with the young founders.
Bell later reported that the deal collapsed because Page wanted Excite to replace its current search system.
The decision was later seen as one of the most costly missed opportunities in technology history.
Today, Google operates as a trillion-dollar company, whereas Excite lost its early market success.

grammar.title: Preposition with Participle Clause
grammar.note: 'Before' acts as a preposition followed by a gerund/participle verb phrase ('becoming...'), creating a concise temporal adverbial.

grammar.title: Participial Phrase as Modifier
grammar.note: An '-ing' participial phrase attached to the end of the clause describes simultaneous secondary action or condition.

grammar.focus: whereas Excite lost its early market success
grammar.title: Contrastive Subordinating Conjunction
grammar.note: 'Whereas' joins two contrasting facts into a single compound sentence to highlight direct differences.

sentences.text: Long before dominating the global technology landscape, Google was nearly sold for a small fraction of its present valuation.
In 1999, Stanford graduate students Larry Page and Sergey Brin felt their search engine project was distracting them from academic studies.
Seeking an exit, the co-founders offered to sell their fledgling search engine to Excite, a leading web portal, for $1 million.
Even after venture capitalist Vinod Khosla negotiated the asking price down to $750,000, Excite chief executive George Bell rejected the deal.
Bell later explained that negotiations stalled primarily because Page insisted that Excite abandon its original search system in favor of Google's algorithm.
Unable to reach an agreement, the two parties walked away, leaving Page and Brin to build their enterprise independently.
Excite subsequently suffered a steep financial decline, whereas Google evolved into a dominant internet powerhouse worth well over $1 trillion.
The rejected transaction remains celebrated as one of the most extraordinary miscalculations in modern commercial history.

grammar.title: Mandative Subjunctive Mood
grammar.note: After verbs of demand like 'insist', the dependent 'that' clause uses the base verb form ('abandon', not 'abandoned' or 'abandons').

grammar.title: Adjectival Participle Pre-modifier
grammar.note: An adjective phrase describing the subject ('the two parties') is placed upfront to set the reason or context for the main action.

grammar.title: Linking Verb with Past Participle Complement
grammar.note: 'Remains' functions as a linking verb followed by a past participle acting as a predicate adjective complement.
